finding: The reversed-guard count moved from one to two this round and is still short by the one that matters most, because the third is not a test literal but a shipped code constant on the agent-facing JSON contract. engine.DivergenceHint (internal/engine/divergence.go:16-19) ends '...; audit convergence still counts every non-PASS row.' — the same clause §4's second guard names in SKILL.md, but here it is a const emitted verbatim as divergence.hint on tp audit --status and tp audit --record. Under blocking the clause is false, and it is false in exactly the situation the object is emitted for: divergence fires when spec-coverage is clean while other roles hold open findings, which is the population blocking exists to stop counting. So an operator who sets blocking is told by tp's own payload that the knob they set does not exist. The constant is pinned in five further places §4 names none of: docs_contract_test.go:145 (assert.Contains(reference, engine.DivergenceHint) — REFERENCE.md:876-880 quotes it in a fenced block), divergence_test.go:166 and :176 (the JSONEq shape), audit_signal_test.go:101, :128 and :303. §4 says 'named as claims rather than as filenames, since an earlier draft scoped the docs by file and the two sentences this release actually falsifies went unnamed for two rounds' — the same defect has now recurred one layer down: a claim, not a file, and it lives in code.
suggestion: Name it as the third reversal and state what it costs: the constant's last clause becomes severity-aware wording true under both values (e.g. '...; audit convergence counts every non-PASS row unless audit_converge_on is blocking'), REFERENCE.md:879's fenced quote moves with it byte-for-byte because docs_contract_test.go:145 compares the document against the constant, and divergence_test.go's JSONEq plus the three audit_signal_test.go assertions read the constant symbolically and need no edit. Add a §5 test asserting the emitted divergence.hint no longer states the unconditional rule; killing input is the shipped constant left unchanged. Alternatively decide the constant is out of scope and say so — but then §4 must stop claiming a count, because 'two guards' is falsified by the same evidence that falsified 'one'.

finding: §4 closes with an exhaustiveness claim over documentation — 'the two sentences this release actually falsifies' — and SKILL.md carries at least two more that blocking makes untrue, neither guarded by any test, so an implementer who works §4's list ships documentation contradicting the feature and nothing reddens. (1) SKILL.md:144, Workflow D step 3: 'a row counts as a finding when status is absent or != PASS; a clean round has zero findings.' Under blocking the second half is flatly false — that is the release's whole content — and this is the sentence a driver agent reads to learn what a clean audit round is. (2) SKILL.md:371: 'An implementation audit always runs to the full 2 consecutive clean rounds and is never cut short by an early cap ... never ship with them open. Implementation correctness is not negotiable.' Under blocking, shipping with warning and info rows open is precisely the sanctioned outcome, so the paragraph forbids the behaviour §2 sells. Neither line is pinned by docs_contract_test.go, so both are silent. By contrast the two §4 does name are the guarded ones — which is the tell: the section enumerated what a test would catch, not what the release falsifies.
suggestion: Replace the count with a list and extend it: SKILL.md:144's clean-round clause, SKILL.md:371's audit-convergence paragraph, SKILL.md:149's divergence clause (docs_contract_test.go:96) and REFERENCE.md's DivergenceHint quote. Or state the scope negatively — 'the release rewords every SKILL.md and REFERENCE.md sentence that asserts audit convergence counts every non-PASS row; the two carrying guards are named because their guards move with them' — which is a rule an implementer can apply to sentences nobody enumerated, rather than a number that goes stale the moment one is missed.

finding: §2 says 'Both write paths are fenced' and names tp set --workflow and its --project form. There is a third supported path to the same task-override layer and it is open under TP_UNATTENDED: tp import. importcmd.go:36-42 fences only --force; a full-TaskFile import writes tf.Workflow straight from the document (importcmd.go:90-93, and the preservation branch at :158-161 only carries the OLD block over when the imported document has no workflow key), so `TP_UNATTENDED=1 tp import tasks.json` with {"workflow":{"audit_converge_on":"blocking"}} exits 0 and persists the relaxing value the fence exists to refuse. §5 test 9 cannot see this: it drives the two set commands only. Two honest qualifications, because the claim should be judged on what is new here. First, the same route already bypasses the cap fence for review_max_rounds, so the hole is a class tp already has rather than one this release invents. Second, that is exactly why it matters now: §2 argues audit_converge_on is 'the first string-valued workflow field whose non-default value relaxes a gate' and that 'the fence is not a detail of this release — it is what the release buys'. A fence a unit walks around by importing is worth less than the section claims, and 'both write paths' is a two-over-an-unenumerated-set claim of the shape CLAUDE.md records five rounds of v0.36.0 falsifying.
suggestion: Either fence it — refuse an imported workflow block carrying audit_converge_on under TP_UNATTENDED, with a third §5 arm whose killing input is a plain (non---force) import of such a document — or scope the claim honestly: 'The two tp set paths are fenced. tp import writes the same layer and is not fenced for any workflow field; closing that is <spec>, not this release.' The first costs one guard at importcmd.go beside the existing --force check; the second costs a sentence and stops §2 asserting a coverage it does not have.

finding: Non-Goal 6 now puts a deliverable in scope — 'The breakdown is in scope and ships on --merge ... a by_severity counter over non-PASS rows' — and it arrives with no test, no field shape, and no home in the release's own description. Three concrete gaps an implementer cannot close by reading. (1) §5 has eleven tests and none touches --merge; §5's closing paragraph claims to enumerate what is deliberately untested and names only role_streaks and spec_coverage_clean_rounds, so by_severity is untested and unlisted, and an implementation that ships without it passes every test in the release. (2) The key set is unspecified. §2's fail-closed rule is stated for the clean PREDICATE, not for a counter, so it does not answer what by_severity does with a row whose severity is null (2,913 PASS rows carry exactly that per §2, though those are excluded here), absent, or out of enum — count it under a synthetic key, under 'error' by the fail-closed analogy, or drop it, which would make the counter's total silently disagree with the summary's own findings count. §2.2's 67 legacy rows guarantee high/medium/low appear in real inputs. (3) --compact is unstated. Non-Goal 6's own citation is ':90-92 already carries a --compact-stripped explanatory key', which reads as an argument that by_severity is stripped too, while REFERENCE.md:641's rule is that decision-critical fields survive and explanatory ones do not — and a breakdown an operator needs to see what blocking suppressed is decision-critical by that rule. Also: §1 still says 'One deliverable', and this is a second one, located inside a Non-Goals section rather than in §2.
suggestion: Move the by_severity paragraph out of Non-Goal 6 into §2 (or its own §2.3) so a deliverable is not specified inside a list of things the release does not do, and pin the three open points: 'by_severity counts non-PASS rows by their severity string; a row whose severity is absent, null or out of enum is counted under the key "unknown"; the counter's values sum to findings; it survives --compact because it is what an operator setting blocking reads to see what was suppressed.' Add a §5 test over a merge input mixing error/warning/info with one out-of-enum and one absent-severity row, killing input a merge that emits by_status and by_role without by_severity. Then fix §1 to say two deliverables, or fold the counter into §2 and keep the count at one.

finding: §2's escalation paragraph makes a counted claim — 'the enum's cardinality is asserted in nine places that must move with it, counted' — and the count is short by at least one, in the file the release must edit anyway. skills/tp/SKILL.md:372 spells the closed set out literally: `tp escalate --decision <skip-gate|raise-review-cap|raise-audit-cap|import-force|other>`. The consuming-validation gap is UNCHANGED: §2 still says only 'rejected with the same hint machinery' and test 2 only 'refused with the same hint shape', with no exit code and no command named, so audit-converge-on-consuming-validation is still the one task whose acceptance I can only write by importing the twin's behaviour rather than by reading this spec. suggestion:
Final import list (id | title | depends_on | acceptance):

1. audit-converge-on-field | Add the audit_converge_on workflow field, its constants and its resolver | [] | audit_converge_on is a presence-tracked field on model.WorkflowOverride and a value on model.Workflow, resolving task override > project config > built-in `all` through engine.ResolveWorkflowLayers with no CLI and no environment layer. engine/auditconvergeon.go mirrors engine/reviewconvergeon.go: two constants, AuditConvergeOnHint = "must be one of: blocking, all", and ValidAuditConvergeOn shared by every caller. The project layer carries it end to end: knownWorkflowKeys gains the key, parseWorkflowOverride gains a string case that does NOT validate at parse time, and WorkflowOverride.IsEmpty gains the field. `tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=<bad>` and its --project form each exit 2 with the hint and leave the file unmodified. Tests 1 and 2 pass, test 2 resolving the project layer through a written .tp/config.json; killing mutation, a resolver reading only the project layer.

Test 3 passes; removing either surface reddens it.

5. audit-converge-on-fence | Fence both tp set write paths under TP_UNATTENDED | ["audit-converge-on-field"] | A third predicate beside engine.FencedCapField and engine.FencedCommandField, with the guard placed before the type dispatch at set.go:361-362 and set_project.go:46-47, so the field never reaches the numeric path. Both values are refused: `audit_converge_on=blocking` and `audit_converge_on=all` each exit 2 under TP_UNATTENDED=1 and 0 without it, at both commands. The refusal has a message of its own — the field is a convergence policy and a user-approved decision — rather than reusing refuseUnattendedCommandField's 'names a command the driver executes'. engine.fencedCapFields and engine/unattended_test.go:69 are untouched. Test 9 passes and fails when either file's guard is missing.

6. audit-converge-on-escalation-name | Add audit-converge-on to the --decision enum and map the field to it | ["audit-converge-on-fence"] | `audit-converge-on` is a constant in engine/escalation.go, a member of escalationDecisions and therefore of IsEscalationDecision, and escalationDecision(field) maps audit_converge_on to it rather than to `other`. cli/escalate_test.go:158's five-literal loop moves with it, and the prose sites are swept: escalation.go's comments, escalation_test.go:60, fakerunner main.go:260, escalate.go:41's help text, REFERENCE.md:347, SKILL.md:247 and SKILL.md:372. Test 10 passes and reddens when the enum entry is removed.

7. audit-converge-on-replay-testdata | Pin §2.1's table as a replay over committed testdata | ["audit-clean-predicate"] | testdata/ carries the per-round (status, severity) rows of v0.35.0's nine and v0.36.0's thirteen recorded audit rounds with the source commit cited in the file. At audit_clean_rounds 2 the predicate reproduces §2.1: blocking converges at round 3 and all at round 9 for v0.35.0; blocking at 3 and all never for v0.36.0. The test reads nothing under spec/.tp-review/. Test 8 passes.

8. audit-converge-on-guard-reversal | Reverse the two test assertions the shipped field invalidates | ["audit-converge-on-field"] | audit_signal_test.go:472-474 asserts that `tp set --workflow --project audit_converge_on=blocking` now exits 0 and persists the value, replacing the two unknown-field assertions. The other nine assert/require calls in TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate are unchanged and pass, including :498's assert.Len(t, e, 3), the wontfix-does-not-clear assertion and the --check-stays-shut assertion; signalRow emits no severity key, so the round stays unclean under the fail-closed rule. Every sentence blocking makes untrue is reworded so it is true under both values, and the guards move with them: SKILL.md:149 with docs_contract_test.go:96's constant, SKILL.md:144's clean-round clause, SKILL.md:371's audit-convergence paragraph, and engine.DivergenceHint with REFERENCE.md:879's fenced quote (docs_contract_test.go:145 compares the document against the constant, so the two must change together).
